# The Iteration 4 pizza data, in full

*Generated by `document_data.py` on 2026-09-20 from the files it describes — do not edit, run the script. Every number, name and flag on this page is read out of the graph, so a topping added to the data shows up here and nowhere has to be remembered.*

**617 triples** in three files: **22 pizzas**, **34 toppings**, **40 facets** a guest can describe a pizza by.

## Where it lives

| file | triples | what it is | written |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data/menu-facts.ttl` | 448 | our own knowledge: the menu, the toppings, the flags | by hand |
| `data/wikidata-links.ttl` | 30 | the curated links to Wikidata, in SKOS | by hand |
| `data/wikidata.ttl` | 139 | what was retrieved through those links | generated by `fetch_wikidata.py` |

One more file in `data/` is not a graph: `wikidata-raw.json`, the raw SPARQL answer the retrieval kept — which is what makes the session work with no network. The documents beside them — `INSTRUCTOR.md`, `wikidata-links.md`, this page — are written for people; the scripts are `fetch_wikidata.py`, `check_facts.py`, `ask.py`, `find_pizza.py` and `document_data.py`.

## The vocabulary

Two classes: **`pz:Pizza`** and **`pz:Topping`**. Everything else is a property. The prefix `pz:` is `http://example.org/pizza/` — the same namespace as Lecture 3's catalog and the lecture's own menu graph, so `pz:Margherita` is one resource across the whole course.

| property | used | of | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pz:hasTopping` | 95× | pizza | what the kitchen puts on this pizza (our authority, never Wikidata's) |
| `rdf:type` | 58× | other, pizza, topping | which class a resource belongs to |
| `pz:name` | 56× | pizza, topping | the canonical name -- what the Pizza API calls it, spelled the same way |
| `pz:externalIngredient` | 51× | pizza | an ingredient *somebody else* lists for the matching item -- never our topping list |
| `pz:alias` | 50× | pizza, topping | another wording a guest may use; several per resource |
| `rdfs:label` | 48× | other | the name of a Wikidata resource, so an answer can say it in words |
| `pz:containsMilk` | 29× | pizza, topping | true when a topping of it contains milk |
| `pz:containsMeat` | 26× | pizza, topping | true when a topping of it contains meat |
| `pz:containsFish` | 25× | pizza, topping | true when a topping of it contains fish or seafood -- separate from meat on purpose |
| `pz:containsEgg` | 23× | pizza, topping | true when a topping of it contains egg |
| `pz:apiId` | 22× | pizza | the id of `GET /pizza` -- the join between the graph and the service |
| `pz:description` | 22× | pizza | one sentence a bot can say out loud |
| `pz:vegan` | 22× | pizza | derived: vegetarian, and no milk and no egg |
| `pz:vegetarian` | 22× | pizza | derived: no meat and no fish |
| `prov:wasDerivedFrom` | 13× | pizza | the Wikidata item the facts in this block were read from |
| `pz:countryOfOrigin` | 10× | pizza | Wikidata's country of origin (P495) |
| `pz:wikipediaArticle` | 9× | pizza | the English Wikipedia article about the matching item |
| `rdfs:comment` | 9× | other, pizza | why this link is what it is -- the reviewer's note |
| `skos:exactMatch` | 9× | pizza | the same thing; facts may be carried over |
| `pz:externalMatch` | 7× | pizza | `pz:NotFound` -- searched, and there is no item. A result, not a gap in the file |
| `skos:closeMatch` | 4× | pizza | the same dish described more generally; read with care |
| `pz:inventedBy` | 2× | pizza | the person Wikidata names as inventor or creator (P61/P170) |
| `skos:relatedMatch` | 2× | pizza | related and *not* the same thing; nothing is carried over |
| `prov:endedAtTime` | 1× | other | when the retrieval ran |
| `prov:used` | 1× | other | the endpoint that was asked |
| `pz:inventedIn` | 1× | pizza | the year Wikidata gives (P571/P575) |

## The toppings

A topping states only what it *does* contain; no statement means "not present". That closed reading is what makes `FILTER NOT EXISTS` in the queries mean what it looks like it means, and it is why the dietary flags on a pizza can be derived at all.

## The external layer

Links: 9 `exactMatch`, 4 `closeMatch`, 2 `relatedMatch`, 7 searched with no item. Facts are read from the first two only — a `relatedMatch` is a link, never a licence to copy.

What the retrieval actually brought back: an inventor for **2 of 22** pizzas (Margherita, Hawaiian), a year for **1** (Hawaiian), a country of origin for **10**, and 51 ingredient statements. That thinness is the lesson, not a defect of the retrieval.

The retrieval ran at **2026-09-20T00:18:12+00:00** against `https://query.wikidata.org/sparql`; the raw answer is `data/wikidata-raw.json`, and every retrieved block carries `prov:wasDerivedFrom` pointing at the item it came from.

The labels of the Wikidata resources our facts point at — inventors, countries, ingredients — are in `wikidata.ttl` too, because an answer has to be able to *say* Sam Panopoulos, not `wd:Q30197020`:

## Keeping this page true

```bash
python3 fetch_wikidata.py     # retrieve again (--offline rebuilds from the cache)
python3 check_facts.py        # flags vs. toppings, ours vs. theirs, the gaps
python3 document_data.py      # rewrite this page
python3 -m pytest -q          # 16 tests, including "every pizza can be found"
```

`document_data.py --check` exits non-zero when the page and the data have drifted apart, which is the check to run before the material is handed out.
